root_cause.text: In `drm/ttm`'s `ttm_bo_shrink()`, the buffer object was removed from the resource bulk-move/LRU tracking before `ttm_tt_backup()` completed, so a backup failure left the resource in an inconsistent LRU state that caused the shrinker to loop indefinitely while walking the LRU.
root_cause.evidence: The patch deletes the pre-backup `ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo)` block and only performs bulk-move removal after successful backup (`if (lret > 0) ... ttm_resource_del_bulk_move_unevictable(bo->resource, bo); ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail(bo->resource);`), while the CVE/commit message explicitly says this fixes an “infinite LRU walk on backup failure.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix shrink-time LRU and bulk-move handling by updating unevictable resources only after a positive backup result instead of removing and re-adding bulk-move state around the backup call.
intent_record.what: The change removes the pre-backup conditional block that, when bo->bulk_move was set, took bdev->lru_lock and called ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo). It also replaces the post-backup conditional from `if (lret <= 0 && bo->bulk_move)` calling ttm_resource_add_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo) to `if (lret > 0)` calling ttm_resource_del_bulk_move_unevictable(bo->resource, bo) and ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail(bo->resource)` under the same lock.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the buffer object is no longer removed from bulk-move tracking before attempting ttm_tt_backup. Instead, only when ttm_tt_backup returns a positive value does the code remove the resource from the unevictable bulk-move state and move it to the tail of the LRU list. This changes the LRU and bulk-move handling around shrink/backup so objects are only repositioned after a successful positive backup outcome, avoiding the old remove-then-readd flow tied to bo->bulk_move.

grouping_result.intent: Fix shrink-time LRU and bulk-move handling by updating unevictable resources only after a positive backup result instead of removing and re-adding bulk-move state around the backup call.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it alters ttm_bo_shrink() so LRU/bulk-move state is updated only after ttm_tt_backup() succeeds, preventing inconsistent LRU tracking when backup fails.

candidates.rationale: This prematurely removes the buffer object's resource from bulk-move/LRU tracking before backup succeeds. If ttm_tt_backup() fails, the resource is left in an inconsistent LRU state, matching the root cause.

The backup operation occurs after the resource was already removed from bulk-move tracking. The ordering of this call relative to the earlier deletion is central to the bug, because failures here leave the LRU state inconsistent.

This condition only restores bulk-move state for lret <= 0, meaning the code first removes tracking unconditionally and then relies on post-backup repair. That repair strategy is what allowed inconsistent state on failure paths per the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the direct root cause: it removes the buffer object's resource from bulk-move/LRU tracking before `ttm_tt_backup()` has succeeded. If the later backup fails, the resource is left in an inconsistent LRU state, which can cause the shrinker to loop indefinitely while walking the LRU.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body clearly shows the relevant logic, so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present because `ttm_bo_shrink()` removes the BO's resource from bulk-move/LRU tracking before calling backup: `if (bo->bulk_move) { ... ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo); ... }` occurs before `lret = ttm_tt_backup(...)`. This matches the root cause: removal happens before backup completion. The reinsertion logic is only done on `if (lret <= 0 && bo->bulk_move) { ... ttm_resource_add_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo); ... }`. That means on successful backup with a positive return value (pages shrunken/purged), the resource stays removed, leaving LRU state changed based solely on the backup outcome path. The commit message itself says `v13: - Take resource off LRU when backed up`, indicating this version intentionally removes it around backup rather than only after confirmed completion. Since the root cause is removing from LRU tracking before `ttm_tt_backup()` completes, and this code does exactly that, the bug is present. The fix is not present because there is no logic to defer `ttm_resource_del_bulk_move()` until after successful backup completion.
